name: portman
description: Keep a registry of the localhost ports each project uses, so dev servers never collide: see what holds each port right now, get free ports that avoid common defaults, find collisions, and write a project's ports to .env.local and a Docker Compose override after you approve

interface.longDescription: Keeps one registry of the localhost ports each of your projects uses, in a file readable only by you, so two dev servers never fight over the same port. It lists every registered port with what holds it right now, a process (named with lsof) or a Docker container, and whether that is the project itself or another program. It suggests free ports that are not registered, not in use, and not a default that popular tools take, such as 3000, 5173, 8000, and 8080. Its doctor finds ports registered twice, registered ports held by another program, and ports in use outside the registry. With your approval of the change it shows, it writes the project's port variables between marker lines in .env.local, leaving every other line as it is, and a Docker Compose override that replaces the published ports. It uses Python, and lsof and docker when they are installed.
defaultPrompt: Find a free port for this project and register it
